title: Long-term kernel_main checklist
summary: Track the path from the current sentinel-and-shutdown kernel_main to the design-doc target: CoreInit, trap shell, reactor/scheduler, VM, subsystem init, and first userspace.

write_sets.notes: Split individual implementation slices into disjoint write sets before parallel work; this plan is the shared long-term checklist.

steps.title: Keep the current H3 kernel_main sentinel baseline green
steps.notes:
Current kernel_main reaches P::init_early, tx_substrate::init::

(), P::init_later, P::install_kernel_trap_vector, prints txkernel:qemu-riscv64-virt:boot:ok, then powers off. Preserve this while replacing the tail with runtime init.

steps.title: Replace sentinel tail with an explicit CoreInit spine
steps.notes: Encode the HAL/PAGE_SUBSTRATE H3 order directly: init_early, substrate::init, init_later, install full trap vector, run post-substrate init hooks, initialize VFS before device, run post-device hooks, initialize reactor/scheduler/subsystems, then enter H4. Keep INIT_HOOKS sparse and never let them reorder substrate, VFS, or device init.

steps.title: Bring up zone, epoch, index, mutation, and bus foundations before semantic subsystems
steps.notes: Implement the substrate pieces upper subsystems assume: epoch::guard, zone::reserve/sign, Weak/IdentRef/Cap/PayloadCap mechanics, persistent index mutation primitives, and RawQueue/RawPort/RawTrace bus carriers with reactor-owned wakers. These must remain substrate mechanisms, not semantic subsystem owners.

steps.title: Replace the panic-only vector with the full trap shell and KernelTrapSink
steps.notes: Implement RawTrapFrame, TrapFrameView, TrapFrameMut, classify-from-frame, user and kernel vector installation, return_to_userspace, and direct named KernelTrapSink methods for page fault, syscall, timer, external IRQ, IPI, and sync fault. Keep trap dispatch out of linkme.

steps.title: Install user-access and kernel-mode fault recovery
steps.notes: Implement UserAccessIf copyin/copyout and the KERNEL_FIXUP_TABLE path for kernel-mode faults. User bytes cross only through this boundary or VM's detached population helper; typed addresses are never raw dereference authority.

steps.title: Publish per-hart state and explicit SMP gates
steps.notes: Define per-hart kernel stack/scratch/TLS state, current task pointer access, AP parked/online states, and a clear single-hart gate for features that do not yet have remote coordination. AP startup may stay disabled until remote shootdown and scheduler handoff land.

steps.title: Implement reactor task table, wait-adapt, wakers, idle, and MVP scheduler
steps.notes: Follow REACTOR_v0 and SCHEDULER_v0: tasks are temporal handles, not entities; steps never call reactor; scripts translate Blocked outcomes into wait-adapt calls; wakers are cheap and do not grant truth; phase-1 scheduler is round-robin with fixed slice and idle when no runnable task exists.

steps.title: Implement VM AddressSpace, recipes, RangeLock, and pmap materialization
steps.notes: Create AddressSpace as a zone entity containing recipes BTree, PmapRoot, RangeLock, and stats. Preserve VM's invariant: pmap PTEs are derived materializations justified by recipes; binding changes linearize at recipes mutation; pmap teardown follows binding withdrawal and shootdown.

steps.title: Complete multi-page, superpage, ASID/global, and remote shootdown accounting
steps.notes: Generalize current page-sized local batches to multi-frame runs, superpage accounting, ASID-scoped and global invalidations, and remote-hart acknowledgment. Until this lands, keep user/VM runtime behind a single-hart gate or explicit no-remote-shootdown mode.

steps.title: Implement PageContainer, RNodeBacking, materialize_page, and reclaim policy hooks
steps.notes: Supply VM's backing model: anonymous zero-fill, file-backed PageContainer materialization, RNodeBacking, cache refs, and reclaim retry policy for non-urgent allocations. Substrate continues to return Exhausted; VM/page-backed decides reclaim and retry.

steps.title: Implement Process, ThreadIdentity/ThreadPayload, and thread_future skeleton
steps.notes: Create the object-model entities and the long-lived thread future. ThreadPayload owns saved user regs, signal mask/summary, pending queues, stop state, child_tid_clear, and TaskHandle; the reactor owns the future, which holds Cap<ThreadPayload>. No per-thread kernel stacks.

steps.title: Add syscall dispatch, page-fault dispatch, and AST return-to-user loop
steps.notes: Implement fixed syscall table dispatch, VM page-fault materializer dispatch, error/return-value writes through TrapFrameMut, and Site B AST handling before user re-entry. Timer preemption should not advance thread_future; interesting traps do.

steps.title: Initialize VFS, tier-1/tier-2 devices, IRQ dispatch, devfs, and console/TTY
steps.notes: Follow DEVICE.md: HAL tier-1 devices remain platform statics; tier-2 static device bindings are enumerated during init; IRQ_HANDLERS are walked once to build an installed dispatch table; devfs exposes device RNodes; console/TTY gets a real userspace-visible path.

steps.title: Build exec loader and detached AddressSpace construction
steps.notes: Implement static-ELF image planning, targeted file reads, detached AddressSpace construction, stack/auxv population, process Frame vm replacement at the point of no return, and ThreadRuntime trap-context install. Keep fallible work before exec's PoNR.

steps.title: Replace kernel_main shutdown with init process spawn and first return_to_userspace
steps.notes: kernel_main should spawn the init thread task, enter the reactor loop, dispatch to userspace through return_to_userspace, and keep the kernel alive until init exits. The old boot sentinel may stay as an early milestone, but successful runtime boot should be a distinct userspace/init sentinel.

steps.title: Enable AP runtime, cross-hart wakeups, IPIs, and remote shootdown
steps.notes: Bring secondary harts online after substrate and before multi-hart scheduling. Install trap vectors on APs, initialize per-hart reactor/scheduler state, support SmpIf IPIs for wake/reschedule/shootdown, and remove the single-hart runtime gate.

steps.title: Add long-running boot tests for shell, BusyBox, and OSComp images
steps.notes: Keep smoke boot separate from runtime boot. Add sentinels for first init entry, first syscall roundtrip, shell prompt, BusyBox command, and OSComp suite readiness as the syscall/VFS/device surface grows.

verification.notes: Use after implementation slices, not required for pure checklist creation.

risks: The current code is substrate-heavy but has no zone/epoch/bus/reactor implementation yet; those are prerequisites for most upper subsystems.
A full trap shell without a VM fault path can only panic or terminate; user execution should stay gated until VM and thread runtime exist.
Remote shootdown and AP scheduling can be deferred for single-hart runtime, but the gate must be explicit to avoid false SMP safety.
Design docs reference many future subsystems; individual implementation slices should refresh readiness before coding from them.
blockers: No implemented zone/entity substrate for upper semantic subsystems yet.
